rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.read: Warsh's last word before Saturday's blackout was no word — 'I don't prejudge meetings' — so October stays ~30% and the meeting is priced as a hold; December pricing split across reads (~67% in one desk recap vs ~90%+ on LSEG Thursday — flagged, not settled). The 10-year fell to ~5.04% in Asia, the softest in about a month. Hammack hardened ('even more' if expectations slip); Macklem leaned hawkish ('harder to look through' energy prices) into Oct 28; Bailey's overnight line was dovish-leaning on the 2027 path while November (~86%+) stands untouched.

rows.title: Growth differentials
rows.figure: NZ PMI 56.5; US IP cons +0.4%; China GDP Mon 4.4%
rows.read: New Zealand's factory pulse is the week's bright spot — BNZ PMI 56.5, strongest since 2021 ex-one spike — while its consumer softened (card spending -0.4%, second fall). Today's US industrial production (consensus +0.4%) is the last hard growth read before the blackout; China's Q3 GDP lands Monday (consensus 4.4% y/y). The US-Europe gap still favors the dollar leg; the antipodean split (NZ factories vs AU jobs) is the regional trade.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US import prices cons +0.8%; EZ final CPI 4am CT
rows.read: Two prints decide the inflation read into the weekend: US import prices at 7:30am CT (consensus +0.8% m/m — the pipeline after PPI's +1.3%) and the eurozone final CPI at 4am CT (confirm-or-revise the 3.8% flash that beat 3.6%). NZ food prices went flat (0.0%) — cooling texture for the RBNZ's two-way Oct 28. What matters is what the banks do about it — and with the Fed in blackout from Saturday, today's prints are the last inputs.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.read: The AI rout faded into a relief bounce: the Nasdaq 100 fell as much as 3.28% intraday Thursday and closed roughly flat (Nasdaq Comp +0.08%, Dow +1.08%) on bargain hunting and falling yields; Asia woke up green (Kospi +3.3%, Nikkei +1.9%). CoreWeave rebounded 6% after Huang's backing (bonds still ~15%); BTC fell below $80k then bounced to ~$82k. Fear idled — the haven bid (gold, CHF) is holding, not extending.

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.read: Escalation and release pulled opposite ways: CENTCOM confirmed an Iranian projectile sank a Hormuz container ship and Houthis hit Aden, while the IEA accelerated ~100M bbl (20M+ diesel ASAP) and the US weighed shadow-fleet sanctions relief — the Brent-WTI spread compressed to ~$8.31 as the freight premium leaked. Hormuz clearance sits at ~68% of baseline. Gold ~$4,172 as the 10-year fell to one-month lows — the anti-dollar bid intact.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: TFF cut: no crowded FX; WTI crowded short (5th)
rows.read: The feed now reads the CFTC Traders in Financial Futures cut (hedge funds & CTAs): no currency is crowded — USD 54th, EUR 44th, GBP 48th, JPY 67th, CHF 41st, CAD 31st, NZD 55th percentile, all neutral signals. The notable split is AUD: hedge funds net long at the 79th while real money sits short at the 17th — the books lean opposite ways. The extreme is in oil: hedge funds crowded short WTI (5th percentile, lightest in 12 weeks) — squeeze potential on a verified supply shock. Next COT lands today.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.read: September's federal budget balance prints at 1pm CT (consensus -$34.7B) — the US fiscal read into the weekend. France: the Oct 20 revenue-section vote and Moody's Oct 23 are the next gates; the EU summit's €100B+ war-driven fossil import bill stands as the euro's winter drag. No new US fiscal development overnight.
